text: Craig Bourne's epistemological objection to the growing block theory contends that:
choices: The theory cannot supply a truthmaker for any proposition about the future
Relativizing pastness to times generates a vicious infinite regress
The present cannot advance at any non-trivial rate without a second time dimension
An agent at the leading edge cannot tell that she is present rather than located in the already-completed interior of the block
explanation: On the growing block, past events remain real, so a past person-stage would have experiences indistinguishable from those at the genuine leading edge; Bourne argues the theory therefore cannot explain how anyone knows she is present rather than embedded in the block's interior. Option 1 is McTaggart's regress and option 2 is the moving spotlight's rate problem -- objections to other positions -- while option 0 misstates the worry as being about future truthmakers rather than self-location.
